record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: Which kinds of social systems should a quantitative model of social resilience investigate, and which kinds should it exclude? The question should account for the authors’ delimitation between society as a system of systems and smaller social organizations or collectives composed of interrelated individuals pursuing a collective goal within an environment.

evidence.quote: Questions • What types of social systems do we want to investigate?
Society is a system of systems, as described above. To understand the resilience of societies requires modeling the interaction of these systems
With the term social organization we refer to formal or informal groups of interrelated individuals who pursue a collective goal and who are embedded into an environment

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider two scales of social aggregation. At the broad scale, a "society" is regarded as a system of systems: a collection S = {S_1, S_2, ..., S_k} of interacting subsystems (e.g., economic, political, cultural, technological) together with a coupling structure describing their mutual interactions. At the finer scale, a "social organization" is a formal or informal group O = (I, G, E) consisting of a set I of interrelated individuals, a collective goal G that the individuals jointly pursue, and an environment E in which the group is embedded.

Develop a principled delimitation criterion that specifies which class of social systems a quantitative model of social resilience should target. Concretely:

(a) Provide a formal definition of the class C of admissible target systems for a quantitative model of social resilience, distinguishing between system-of-systems societies and goal-directed organizations of interrelated individuals.

(b) State, with justification, which kinds of social systems must be excluded from C (for instance, aggregates lacking a shared collective goal, transient crowds, or systems without an identifiable environment), and characterize the boundary cases.

(c) For the admissible class C, specify the minimal structural ingredients (agents, interactions, goals, environment, observables) that any quantitative resilience model must incorporate, and argue why these ingredients are both necessary and sufficient to make the notion of resilience well-defined and measurable.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a conceptual delimitation problem for modeling social resilience rather than a fully formalized mathematical conjecture. It is posed as an open question for the research community, and no consensus formal answer appears to exist in the literature on quantitative social-resilience modeling.

status_evidence.title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
status_evidence.snippet: A survey identifying open questions about quantitative modeling of social resilience, including which social systems should be targeted.
status_evidence.claim: The delimitation of target social systems is explicitly framed as an open methodological question without a settled answer.
